<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #46945

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [x] Unit test
- [x] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [ ] No code

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note
None
```

issue_context.title: Use `tk.MustHasPlan` and `tk.MustNotHasPlan` instead of `tk.HasPlan`
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement
The function `tk.HasPlan` will return a bool var indicates whether is has required plan or not.

But sometimes developer miss check the results like https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/061a1391f2c0a379797c486a74124184caefc6f3/expression/integration_serial_test/integration_serial_test.go#L530

For example, the test case `TestCollateIndexLookup`, although its result has changed, we did not find it through UT.

review_comments: Oh, this was indeed bad usage :) (when the correct one was below...)
Should the message part also be kept, or should the message in Must[Not]HavePlan also include the full Explain, to see the full plan as well as what was expected?
Should these return "TableFullScan" or something else? Maybe the cases struct could be extended with matching MustHavePlan/MustNotHavePlan?
Yes, it's `TableFullScan`. Not sure it should be checked in this test or not.
